title: Northern National Bank vs Meridian Realty Pvt Ltd & Ors
nextHearingPurpose: Cross-examination of Bank's Chief Manager on NPA classification date

facts.fact: Original sanction letter dated 14 Oct 2019 provided 24 months construction moratorium which was improperly curtailed to 18 months in revised sanction.
Bank classified account as NPA on 31 Dec 2023 despite receiving interest payments of ₹ 4.50 Cr on 28 Dec 2023.
Recovery Officer issued provisional attachment order over Panvel Parcel P-004 on 14 Feb 2026 without prior show cause.

timeline.title: Original Application OA 142/2025 filed at DRT-I
Provisional Attachment Warrant issued for Panvel Land
Written Statement filed by Meridian Realty

conflicts.title: NPA Classification Date Discrepancy
conflicts.sideA: Bank asserts default occurred on 30 Sep 2023 based on 90-day overdue rule.
conflicts.sideB: Bank's own account statement shows RTGS credit of ₹ 4.50 Cr credited on 28 Dec 2023, curing the 90-day trigger.

otherSideArguments.point: Borrower failed to deposit milestone escrow collections directly into designated trap account as mandated by Clause 9 of the facility agreement.
Corporate guarantor Meridian Infra Holdings Ltd has not honoured notice of invocation issued in April 2024.

strengths: Documentary proof of timely RTGS interest payment before NPA date.
Clear breach of RBI master circular on NPA classification guidelines.
Solvent collateral value: Hinjewadi & Panvel parcels exceed ₹ 230 Cr against claim of ₹ 112.40 Cr.
weaknesses: Escrow account turnover showed occasional delays during monsoon quarters.
High penal interest accumulation of ₹ 9.10 Cr adds compounding burden.

missingInfo.item: Certified copy of Bank Sanction Committee Minutes for Moratorium Revision
DRT Valuer's Report on Hinjewadi Land valuation

hearings.purpose: Arguments on Interim Injunction against auction
hearings.outcome: Auction stayed subject to verification of statement of account

title: Civil Title Suit: Mirza Asad Baig Legal Heirs vs Sunrise Developers Pvt Ltd
nextHearingPurpose: Hearing on IA No. 4/2025 (Temporary Injunction restraining construction)

facts.fact: Plaintiffs claim ancestral title through 1954 Inam grant claiming Survey 89/2 was Maqta land not extinguished by Inams Abolition Act.
Special Chief Secretary Revenue, Telangana affirmed Ryotwari Patta issued to vendor's predecessor in 1978 under Section 4 of Inams Act.

timeline.title: Purchase of Survey 89/2 (22 acres) by Sunrise Developers
Plaint filed in OS 891/2025 claiming partition and declaration
Written Statement filed proving 45 years peaceful possession

conflicts.title: Nature of Inam Grant (Personal Inam vs Service Inam)
conflicts.sideA: Plaintiffs allege land was Madad-e-Maash inam protected under religious trust exemptions.
conflicts.sideB: Revenue records and Nazim Atiyat orders prove absolute conversion to patta land in 1978.

otherSideArguments.point: The succession of original inamdar was never formally sanctioned under Atiyat proceedings.

strengths: Consistent mutation entries in Dharani portal and registered sale deeds dating back 45 years.
Clear precedent of Telangana High Court upholding Section 4 Patta in identical neighbouring survey numbers.
weaknesses: Temporary stay on construction might delay financing draws from Coastal Finance Ltd.

missingInfo.item: Certified copy of 1978 Nazim Atiyat order from State Archives Hyderabad

hearings.bench: VI Addl Senior Civil Judge, Hyderabad

title: Zenith Infra Projects vs Meridian Infra Holdings Ltd (IBC S.9)
nextHearingPurpose: Reporting of consent terms / withdrawal under Section 12A IBC

facts.fact: Operational creditor claimed unpaid invoices of ₹ 4.82 Cr for structural steel supply at Lower Parel site.
Pre-existing dispute was raised via email dated 12 Dec 2025 citing laboratory rejection of sub-standard steel tensile strength.

timeline.title: Operational Creditor Demand Notice under Section 8 IBC
Section 9 Petition filed at NCLT Mumbai
Bipartite settlement talks concluded at ₹ 3.20 Cr in two tranches

otherSideArguments.point: Delivery challans were signed by project supervisor without remark at time of unloading.

strengths: Clear pre-existing dispute prior to receipt of Section 8 notice (Mobilox Innovations test satisfied).
Draft consent terms agreed; awaiting final Board approval and first tranche release.

hearings.bench: Judicial Member & Technical Member, NCLT Bench-II

title: Meridian Infra Holdings vs State of Maharashtra (Land Acquisition Reference)
nextHearingPurpose: Final hearing on compensation enhancement under RFCTLARR Act 2013

facts.fact: Special Land Acquisition Officer awarded ₹ 42 Lakh/acre against prevailing market rate of ₹ 1.60 Cr/acre.

timeline.title: Section 11 Preliminary Notification for Highway Widening
Writ Petition filed challenging inadequate award

otherSideArguments.point: State claims agricultural index rate must apply rather than commercial development potential.

strengths: Comparable sale deeds of adjacent industrial corridors within 500 meters justify ₹ 1.60 Cr/acre.

strengths: Prior approved sanctions created vested developmental rights.

title: Om Logistics vs Meridian Infra Holdings (S.138 NI Act)

facts.fact: Cheque of ₹ 65 Lakhs was issued as security and banked without authorization after dispute.

otherSideArguments.point: Signed cheque constitutes legally enforceable debt under S.139 presumption.

strengths: Complainant agreed in writing to compound upon ₹ 55 Lakh payment.
